children: U.S. Treasury yields recover from their pre-Thanksgiving retreat and move higher as equities post Black Friday gains and the U.S. dollar strengthens. Data in the holiday-shortened week included an upward revision in U.S. 3Q GDP and a PCE inflation reading in line with estimates, which supported strong expectations the Fed will raise interest rates on Dec. 9. "The Fed still has a long way to go to get inflation back to its 2% target," Brown Brothers Harriman says in a note. An equity correction alone is unlikely to stop the Fed from tightening, the firm says. "The Fed's hawkish policy stance is intact and supportive of USD." The 10-year Treasury yield rises 8.7 basis points to 4.933%, up 2.4 basis points on the week. (anthony.harrup@wsj.com)
